skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

llm.summary: This skill appears to analyze pet feeding videos, but it also silently creates or reuses an identity, logs in or registers with a backend, stores tokens locally, and sends video plus identity data to cloud APIs.

dimensions.detail: The cloud video-analysis and history-report features fit the stated purpose, but the artifacts expand beyond analysis into automatic identity resolution, silent account login/registration, token handling, local user persistence, and cloud history access.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent to handle identity internally, not ask the user for identity values, and automatically query cloud history on broad report-related phrases; --open-id and --api-key are also suppressed in CLI help.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install-time script or destructive install behavior was found. Dependencies are ordinary Python libraries, but the package does not provide a clear permissions/privacy section and includes an inactive dev config pointing at private raw IP services.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: For a pet-video skill, reading OpenClaw sender/workspace identity, reading workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt, uploading local videos or remote URLs, and attaching tenant/skill/user metadata to backend requests is sensitive and not clearly gated by user consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The common code creates a workspace data directory and SQLite database, creates or reuses a default user, and stores token/open_token fields in sys_user for later requests.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. Use it only if you are comfortable sending pet-feeding videos or supplied video URLs to the Lifeemergence backend and having the skill silently create or reuse an identity, query identity-linked report history, and store backend tokens in a local workspace SQLite database. Avoid sensitive home, clinic, or boarding-facility footage unless the publisher's privacy and retention terms are acceptable.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Network calls, file reads/uploads, local output, and shell-invoked scripts are expected for this cloud analysis skill, but the lack of a consolidated permissions/privacy disclosure is a real under-disclosure issue.
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in substance: automatic account lifecycle, token storage, and identity-linked history materially expand the trust boundary beyond straightforward video analysis.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in substance for silent identity creation/reuse, hidden identity parameters, identity-scoped history retrieval, and stored token/open_token fields; these are high-impact without clear user control.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Partly accepted: generic CRUD and HTTP wrappers are common shared-code patterns, but they are broader than this skill needs and compound the identity/token concerns.
[SQP-1] expected: History lookup is documented, but automatic triggering on broad report phrases without confirmation can expose account-linked prior reports unintentionally.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending videos or URLs to server-side APIs is expected and disclosed in the description, but the skill lacks clear user-facing consent, retention, and identity-metadata disclosure.
[E1] unexpected: Accepted as sensitive outbound identity transmission: the code posts openId/mobile/source to a backend login endpoint with silent registration enabled; no evidence shows unrelated theft, so this supports Review rather than malicious.
[AST7] expected: Downgraded: dynamic getattr is in a local generic SQLAlchemy DAO and is not shown as externally exposed in this skill path, though it remains weaker than allowlisted filters.
[P2] expected: Downgraded: the detected U+200D is part of a visible emoji sequence in SKILL.md, not concealed operational text.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded as an automatic metadata-pattern hit; the operational manifest is broad, but the actionable concern is the separately verified identity/account/token behavior.
[static:suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: Downgraded: the raw private IP appears only in config-dev.yaml, while default config.yaml selects prod public HTTPS endpoints; it is still worth removing or clearly labeling dev-only config.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean and does not add negative signal.
